title: Pay conditioning and precision before claiming finite expected bit work
statement: For the fixed Maxwell prototype a=1,b=11/10, bin width1/4 and each fixed rational t>=0, the acquired derivation pays marked genealogy/raw loops, occupied child norms, Gaussian inversion, reused factory thresholds and final floors. A constructive iterative elementary-interval evaluator with polynomial precision/expression/argument-height costs then has finite expected fair-bit and bit work. This is not uniform-in-time complexity or an expected CPU bound for a particular Arb build.
